title: Architecture & sequence-length aware execution-plan tuner for runtime kernels
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an online autotuner that produces an execution plan for decoding/prefill that picks the best low-level kernels and scheduling strategy given (a) hardware fingerprint (GPU architecture, compute capability, memory layout), (b) sequence-length distributions for a customer workload, and (c) latency/cost SLOs.

Scope: prototype an algorithm that 1) warm-starts from offline profiler maps, 2) uses short online probes plus lightweight Bayesian/bandit updates to switch plans, and 3) enforces safety constraints (latency p95 guardrail, memory headroom). The tuner must operate per-tenant and per-model variant and feed decisions into the runtime planning layer (batching geometry, kernel variant, attention tiling, KV placement).

Design highlights:
- Offline stage: generate a matrix of candidate execution plans by combining kernel variants (e.g., fused attention, block-sparse tiling, flash variants), attention implementation choices (causal vs chunked), and KV cache strategies. Profile each candidate across representative seq-lens on known architectures; compress results into a small fingerprint map keyed by (arch, batch, seqlen-quantile).
- Warm-start: on new hardware/tenant, load nearest-match profiles (by arch family) and use them to initialize the priors for the online tuner.
- Online stage: for steady workload, execute lightweight probes periodically and run a hierarchical multi-armed bandit: first choose attention-family (fast-fusion vs memory-friendly), then choose kernel variant and batching plan. Use Thompson sampling with a cost-penalty factor to bias toward lower-cost options when multiple options have similar latency.
- Safety & rollout: only switch plans if expected improvement > 8% p95 or >12% cost reduction while respecting memory slack. Implement canary: 5% traffic ramp for 30 minutes with rollback threshold at +5% p95 degradation.
- Observability: expose per-plan metrics (latency p50/p95, cost-per-token estimate, OOM counts) to Console; store plan fingerprints in model metadata for offline analysis.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end prototype that picks plans and demonstrates >10% cost reduction on two internal seq-len skewed workloads without p95 regressions.
- Integration with runtime planner to apply decisions per-route.
- Console dashboard panels for plan-level metrics and a runbook describing rollback.

Non-goals: full search over quantization profiles or training-time model changes. This ticket focuses on runtime kernel/attention selection and scheduling only.

2026-03-03 - Lena Schmidt (review): Reviewed safety model. Suggested tightening canary to 3% traffic for first 15 minutes, then 5% if stable. Also requested memory headroom metric exported from allocator. Filed follow-up ENG-25702 to add allocator metrics.

2026-03-06 - Marco Nguyen: Implemented warm-start lookup and Bandit controller prototype. On internal benchmark for 'summarization-stream' workload, cost per token dropped ~11% with unchanged p95. Benchmark notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1X-probes

2026-03-09 - QA (Diego Alvarez): Running fuzz tests with adversarial bursts. Found one regression: for seqlen=2048, certain plan switches cause transient OOMs under bursty load. Mitigation: add a conservative memory margin multiplier (x1.2) and increase probe frequency temporarily after large seqlen jump. Added to checklist.
